name: LTC4364HDE-2#PBF
title: LTC4364-1/LTC4364-2: surge stopper with ideal diode controller, 4 V to 80 V, DFN-14, MSOP-16 and SO-16
summary: A controller for two external N-channel MOSFETs that protects a load from input surges, overcurrent and reversed supplies. The first MOSFET regulates the output to a level set by a divider on FB during an overvoltage and limits current through a sense resistor; an adjustable fault timer, shortened as the MOSFET's drop rises, turns it off if the fault lasts. The second MOSFET is an ideal diode with a 30 mV regulated drop that blocks reverse current and holds the output up through brownouts and input shorts. The LTC4364-1 latches off after a fault; the LTC4364-2 retries after a cool-down at about 0.1 % duty cycle.
key_figures: 50 mV typ (25 mV with OUT below 1.5 V)
10 V to 16 V for VCC 8 V to 80 V
370 µA typ; 10 µA typ in shutdown
C 0 °C to 70 °C, I –40 °C to 85 °C, H –40 °C to 125 °C

notes: -1 latches off after a fault; -2 restarts automatically after the cool-down. The temperature grade (C, I, H) is shown on a label on the shipping container. Some packages also come in 500-unit reels with a #TRMPBF suffix. #W parts are built under controlled manufacturing for automotive use and are the grades offered for automotive applications. The part is AEC-Q100 qualified for automotive applications.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Senses the output, at the drain of the ideal-diode MOSFET. The difference VCC − OUT sets the fault timer current; once OUT comes within 0.7 V of VCC, ENOUT goes high impedance. Needs at least 22 µF of low-ESR electrolytic bypass.

pins.name: SENSE
pins.function: Current sense input, taken to the input end of the sense resistor whose other end is OUT. The current loop drives HGATE to hold SENSE − OUT at 50 mV while OUT is above 2.5 V and at 25 mV once OUT is below 1.5 V; the same amplifier starts the TMR charging current. SENSE − OUT must stay under 30 V. Tie to OUT when unused.

pins.name: DGATE
pins.function: Gate drive for the ideal-diode MOSFET. With more than 30 mV across that MOSFET an internal charge-pump current pulls DGATE up, clamped 12 V above SOURCE; at light load it is servoed to keep 30 mV across it. Reverse current brings a 130 mA pull-down to SOURCE. DGATE stays low with VCC unpowered or below ground while the output is held up. On supplies of 24 V or more add a 15 V Zener from DGATE to SOURCE. Tie to SOURCE or leave open when unused.

pins.name: SOURCE
pins.function: Common source of the two back-to-back N-channel MOSFETs, and the return for both gate drivers; connect it directly to their sources. It is the ideal diode's anode: the voltage from SOURCE to SENSE is the diode's forward drop that DGATE regulates.

pins.name: HGATE
pins.function: Gate drive for the surge-stopper MOSFET, pulled up by an internal charge-pump current and clamped 12 V above SOURCE. The voltage and current amplifiers both act on it to limit the output voltage and the MOSFET current. Needs 6.8 nF or more from HGATE to GND; on supplies of 24 V or more add a 15 V Zener from HGATE to SOURCE.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply input, 4 V to 80 V in operation; it tolerates being taken 40 V below ground by a reversed battery. Shutdown through SHDN drops its current to 10 µA.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Shutdown input. Below 0.5 V the part turns off and VCC current falls to 10 µA; above 2.2 V, or left open, an internal current source turns it back on. Open, it is clamped internally at 4 V; without a pull-up, leakage to ground at this pin must not exceed 1 µA. Withstands 100 V and 40 V below GND.

pins.name: UV
pins.function: Undervoltage comparator input. Below 1.25 V, HGATE is pulled down by 1 mA; above 1.25 V plus the hysteresis, the charge pump pulls HGATE up again. On the LTC4364-1, taking UV below 0.6 V after a latch-off clears the latch and lets HGATE retry. Tie to SHDN when unused.

pins.name: OV
pins.function: Overvoltage comparator input. Above 1.25 V it blocks fault retry; below 1.25 V HGATE may turn on again once the fault has cleared. At power-up, OV above its threshold keeps the HGATE MOSFET off. Tie to GND when unused.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Device ground.

pins.name: FLT
pins.function: Open-drain fault output, active low, needing an external pull-up resistor or current source. It goes low once TMR reaches the 1.25 V warning threshold, meaning the HGATE MOSFET is about to turn off for a lasting overvoltage or an overcurrent. Sinks up to 2 mA; withstands 80 V. Tie to GND or leave open when unused.

pins.name: ENOUT
pins.function: Open-drain enable output, needing a pull-up resistor or current source to OUT. It goes high impedance when OUT is above VCC − 0.7 V, meaning the external MOSFETs are fully on; that state is latched and clears when OUT falls below 2.2 V. Sinks up to 2 mA; withstands 80 V. Tie to GND or leave open when unused.

pins.name: TMR
pins.function: Fault timer. A capacitor to ground, accurate and with low voltage and temperature coefficients, sets the warning time, the turn-off time and the cool-down time. Voltage or current regulation starts charging it with a current that grows with VCC − OUT. At 1.25 V FLT goes low; at 1.35 V the HGATE MOSFET turns off. When the fault is gone TMR swings 32 times between 0.15 V and 1.35 V at 2 µA; after the 32nd fall past 0.15 V the LTC4364-2 lets HGATE turn on again if OV is below its threshold, while the LTC4364-1 stays latched off.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input of the output voltage regulator, from a divider between OUT and ground. During an overvoltage HGATE is driven to hold FB at 1.25 V. Tie to GND to disable the output clamp.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: Exposed pad; connecting it to GND is optional.

circuits.title: 4 A, 12 V overvoltage output regulator with ideal diode, rated for a 200 V 1 ms input transient
circuits.description: A 12 V supply reaches the load through M1, the surge-stopper MOSFET, and M2, the ideal-diode MOSFET, which share a source node; a 10 mΩ resistor after M2 senses the load current for the current limit. When the input surges, the 102k/4.99k divider on FB holds the output at about 27 V. The 2.2k resistor and the 68 V Zener feed and clamp VCC, with SHDN tied to VCC so the part is always enabled. The 383k/90.9k/10k string on the input sets the undervoltage level at 6 V and the overvoltage level at 60 V. 6.8 nF on HGATE compensates the gate loop, 0.22 µF on TMR sets the fault timer, and ENOUT and FLT report the output state.

circuits.title: Figure 1. 4 A, 12 V overvoltage output regulator with reverse current protection
circuits.description: The worked design example: a 12 V input (8 V to 14 V DC) feeding a 4 A load, with the output held to 27 V during surges, a 4 A minimum current limit, a 6 V low-battery level, a 60 V input overvoltage level and 1 ms of early warning before turn-off. D3 and D4 are a back-to-back transient-suppressor pair on the input: D3 limits positive transients to 200 V and D4 limits how far below ground the source node can go. R4 and C1 filter VCC and, with the 68 V Zener D1, clamp it during a surge. R5 in series with M1's gate, and R6 with D5 in series with CHG, set the HGATE loop: D5 lets a fast input step reach CHG directly. R9 pulls ENOUT up to the output.
notes: UV = 6 V and OV = 60 V are set by R1, R2 and R3.

circuits.title: Figure 2. Separate filtered UV and OV dividers that block start-up into an overvoltage
circuits.description: Two independent dividers from the input drive the UV and OV pins, each with its own filter capacitor. The UV divider (383k over 100k) trips at 6 V and the OV divider (475k over 10k) at 60 V. The UV time constant, (383k||100k) × 10 nF, is far longer than the OV one, (475k||10k) × 1 nF, so when a board is plugged into a supply above 60 V the OV pin rises past its threshold before UV releases, and the pass MOSFETs stay off until the supply falls below 60 V.

circuits.title: Figure 7a. VCC fed through a depletion-mode N-channel MOSFET
circuits.description: For an input that stays high for a long time, a depletion-mode MOSFET with its gate tied to its source replaces the VCC series resistor, whose dissipation would otherwise be too high. The 68 V Zener D1 clamps VCC and C1 bypasses it; the input may peak at 200 V.

circuits.title: Figure 7b. VCC fed through an NPN emitter follower
circuits.description: An NPN transistor buffers the VCC supply: R4 feeds its base from the input, the 68 V Zener D1 clamps the base, and the emitter feeds VCC. The input can reach 200 V peak. To survive a reversed supply the collector is blocked with a series diode or taken to the cathode of the input transient suppressors.

circuits.title: Figure 8. 2 A wide-range hot swap controller with circuit breaker
circuits.description: A single MOSFET hot swap for 5 V to 28 V with no ideal diode: SOURCE and SENSE share the node between M1 and the 20 mΩ sense resistor, DGATE is left open, and FB is grounded so the output clamp is off. The 118k/44.2k/5.9k string sets UV at 4.2 V and OV at 36 V. CHG (47 nF) slows the HGATE ramp to limit inrush into the 100 µF load, the 15 V Zener D6 protects M1's gate-source junction, and the SMAT70A suppressor on the input clamps transients. SHDN, ENOUT and FLT are open.

circuits.title: Figure 9. 28 V hot swap with output regulation at 36 V, circuit breaker and reverse current protection
circuits.description: An 18 V to 33 V supply passes through M1 and the ideal-diode MOSFET M2 to a 2.5 A load. R7 (110k) over R8 (4.02k) clamps the output at 36 V during a surge; the 100k/6.04k/3.01k string sets UV at 15 V and OV at 45 V. VCC is tied straight to the input and SHDN is open. Each MOSFET has a 15 V Zener from gate to source (D6 on M1, D7 on M2), as asked for on supplies of 24 V or more. ENOUT and FLT are open.

circuits.title: Figure 10. 48 V hot swap with output regulation at 72 V, circuit breaker and reverse current protection
circuits.description: A 36 V to 72 V supply feeds a 4 A load through M1 and the ideal-diode MOSFET M2, with a 10 mΩ sense resistor. R7 (226k) over R8 (4.02k) clamps the output at 72 V. VCC is fed through 2.2k and clamped by a 68 V Zener, with SHDN tied to VCC. The 205k/3.92k/3.48k string sets UV at 36 V and OV at 76 V. 15 V Zeners protect both gates. ENOUT and FLT are open.

circuits.title: Figure 11. Redundant supply diode-OR with overvoltage surge protection
circuits.description: Two 12 V supplies, A and B, each have their own LTC4364, pass MOSFET, ideal-diode MOSFET and 10 mΩ sense resistor, and join at one common output. The ideal diodes keep either supply from feeding the other. On each side the 59k/4.99k divider runs from the SOURCE node, not from the shared output, and the output is clamped at 16 V. VCC, SHDN and UV of each controller sit on its own input, OV is grounded, and 0.22 µF on each TMR pin sets the fault timer. ENOUT and FLT are open.

circuits.title: Figure 12. High side switch with ideal diode for load protection
circuits.description: The part used as a plain switch: M1 turns the 12 V supply on and off and M2 blocks reverse current from the load side. There is no sense resistor (SENSE is tied to OUT), FB is grounded so there is no output clamp, and OV and TMR are grounded. SHDN and UV share a node pulled up to the input by 100k; driving the gate of M3 high pulls that node to ground and turns the switch off.

circuits.title: Figure 13. Overvoltage regulator with output keep alive during shutdown
circuits.description: A 12 V, 4 A surge stopper whose output is not left dead when the MOSFETs are off: R9 (1k, 1 W) runs from the input straight to the output and the 18 V, 1 W Zener D8 across the output limits that path's voltage. R7 (287k) over R8 (24.9k) clamps the output at 16 V. VCC is fed through 2.2k with a 68 V Zener, SHDN tied to VCC; the 191k/40.2k/10k string sets UV at 6 V and OV at 30 V.

circuits.title: Figure 14. 250 mA high-voltage low-dropout linear regulator with current limit and reverse current protection
circuits.description: From a 20 V input, R2 (182k) over R3 (21k) on FB sets the output at 12 V, and the 0.15 Ω sense resistor limits the current. M2 blocks reverse current. VCC, SHDN and UV sit on the input; OV and TMR are grounded. Its response to a load step is slow, set by the internal charge pump.
notes: The output's load-step response is slow because of the internal charge pump's response time.

circuits.title: Figure 15. Overvoltage regulator with reverse input protection to -70 V
circuits.description: The controller's own ground (GND pin, the UV/OV string, the FB divider, CHG, CTMR and the VCC Zener) returns to system ground through M3. M3's gate is fed from the input through R6 (100k) and clamped to its source by the 12 V Zener D3. The bidirectional suppressor D1 clamps the input. The rest is a 12 V, 6.5 A surge stopper with the output clamped at 16 V (59k over 4.99k), UV at 6 V and OV at 60 V.
notes: ICGND is the controller's local ground, joined to system ground through M3.

circuits.title: Figure 16. 0.25 A, 12 V surge stopper with output port protection
circuits.description: The output goes to a connector, so it may be plugged into another supply, including one below ground. The output is held to 18 V by R7, R9 and R8 (49.9k, 16.9k, 4.99k); the 15 V Zener D2 runs from the R7/R9 junction to ground. Only ceramic capacitors bypass the output (two 10 µF, 50 V), with a 100 mΩ resistor in series with them for stability at light load. The port is protected against backfeeding or forward conduction from -20 V to 50 V.

parts.value: clamped at 18V; port protected from -20V to 50V

equations.name: Sense resistor

where.ΔVSNS: overcurrent threshold, 50 mV typ with OUT above 2.5 V

equations.note: The design example uses the 45 mV minimum: 45 mV / 4 A = 11 mΩ, and 10 mΩ is chosen.

equations.name: Overvoltage timer current
equations.note: About 2 µA at 0.5 V or less across the MOSFETs, rising to 50 µA at 75 V.

equations.name: Overcurrent timer current
equations.note: 10 µA at 0.5 V or less, rising to 260 µA at 75 V.

equations.name: Early warning time
equations.note: Time from FLT going low to M1 turning off in an overvoltage fault.

equations.name: Overcurrent fault on-time
equations.note: In the design example (CTMR = 47 nF, VCC = 14 V, VOUT = 0 V, ITMR(UP) = 55 µA) tOC = 1.15 ms; with VOUT = 2 V and 49 µA, 1.3 ms. The denominator reads ITRM(UP); it is ITMR(UP).

equations.name: MOSFET stress for the prototypical transient
equations.expr: P²t = ILOAD² × [ (1/3) × tr × (b − a)³ / b + (1/2) × τ × (2a² × ln(b/a) + 3a² + b² − 4ab) ]

equations.name: MOSFET stress, simplified
equations.note: For VREG ≈ VIN and τ ≫ tr. VPK = 80 V, VIN = 12 V, VREG = 16 V, tr = 10 µs, τ = 1 ms and 3 A give 18.4 W²s.

equations.name: Short-circuit stress
equations.note: VIN = 15 V, OUT = 0 V, ΔVSNS = 25 mV, RSNS = 12 mΩ, CTMR = 100 nF give 2.2 W²s; doubled to 4.4 W²s for tolerances.

equations.name: Output clamp voltage
equations.note: Design example: 250 µA in the divider gives R8 = 5k (4.99k chosen) and R7 = (27V − 1.25V) × R8 / 1.25V = 102.8k (102k chosen).

equations.name: Largest VCC series resistor
equations.note: 2.2k is chosen. With a 64 V minimum Zener voltage the peak Zener current in a 200 V surge is (200V − 64V) / 2.2k = 62 mA.

equations.name: Timer capacitor for early warning
equations.note: 1 ms gives 50 nF; 47 nF is chosen.

equations.name: UV and OV divider
equations.note: With R3 = 10k: R2 = (60V/6V − 1) × R3 = 90k and R1 = (6V/1.25V − 1) × (R2 + R3) = 380k; 90.9k and 383k are chosen.

equations.name: Pass MOSFET dissipation in current limit
equations.note: 14 V × 32 mV / 10 mΩ = 45 W (P²t 2.3 W²s) into a dead short; with VOUT at 2 V, (14V − 2V) × 55 mV / 10 mΩ = 66 W (P²t 5.7 W²s).

operation.text: The LTC4364 drives two external N-channel MOSFETs in series: M1, the pass device of an overvoltage regulator, and M2, an ideal diode that blocks reverse current and holds the output up. It runs from 4 V to 80 V on VCC; a clamp on VCC lets the input itself go higher, and VCC may be pulled 40 V below ground. In normal running M1 is fully on and dissipates very little.

When the input surges, the voltage amplifier takes over M1's gate and servoes OUT so that FB sits at the internal 1.25 V reference, the level being set by the divider from OUT. M1 stays on and the load keeps running through brief transients. If regulation lasts past the timer period, an overvoltage fault is declared and HGATE is pulled to SOURCE by 1 mA.

The current amplifier regulates M1's gate so that the voltage across the sense resistor between SENSE and OUT is 50 mV with OUT above 2.5 V, falling to 25 mV with OUT below 1.5 V to ease the stress in a hard short. If limiting lasts past the timer period, HGATE is pulled to SOURCE by 1 mA at once.

The TMR capacitor is charged by a current while an overvoltage or overcurrent lasts. The current depends on VCC − VOUT, the drop across M1, so the timeout shortens as M1's stress grows; in overcurrent it is five times the overvoltage value. At 1.25 V FLT goes low as a warning; in an overvoltage fault the current then falls to a fixed 5 µA, giving a constant warning interval, while in overcurrent it stays high. At 1.35 V M1 turns off. If the fault clears between 1.25 V and 1.35 V, TMR discharges at 2 µA and FLT returns high impedance when TMR reaches 0.15 V.

After turn-off, TMR discharges at 2 µA to 0.15 V, charges at 2 µA to 1.35 V, and repeats 32 times. At the end the OV pin is checked: above 1.25 V retry is held off; below 1.25 V minus the hysteresis the LTC4364-2 turns M1 back on and FLT goes high impedance. The retry duty cycle is about 0.1 %. The LTC4364-1 produces the same pulses but stays latched off with FLT low.

The LTC4364-1 restarts after a UV pulse below 0.6 V lasting more than 10 µs, applied after the cool-down; applied during the cool-down it leaves the pulses alone and the part restarts when the cool-down ends. A SHDN pulse low for more than 200 µs also restarts either version: during the cool-down it discharges TMR with 1 mA and restart follows when TMR is below 0.15 V; after the cool-down restart is immediate. OV above 1.25 V blocks either restart until it falls. A UV pulse does nothing on the LTC4364-2. Enough cool-down time should pass before toggling SHDN.

The OV pin, through a divider from the input, does not turn M1 off once HGATE has begun to rise; it only prevents restart after a fault, so the pass device does not cycle on and off while the input stays high. At power-up, OV above 1.25 V while the 100 µs power-on reset is still running, or before UV clears, keeps HGATE low until OV falls. Separate UV and OV dividers with filter capacitors, τUV / τOV above 50, keep the part from starting when hot-plugged into an overvoltage.
With UV below 1.25 V, HGATE and DGATE are held low. When UV rises past 1.25 V plus 50 mV typical hysteresis, HGATE is released without a timer cycle. Undervoltage does not pull FLT low.

ENOUT goes high impedance when OUT reaches within 0.7 V of VCC during start-up, and stays latched until OUT falls below 2.2 V. With OUT below 1 V the open-drain output loses its ability to keep ENOUT low when the pull-up returns to a separate supply; with the pull-up to OUT and at least 100k, ENOUT stays below 0.6 V typical. A level shifter can drive lower-voltage logic.

M2's source and drain are the diode's anode and cathode. DGATE is servoed for 30 mV forward drop; with M2 fully on and the drop above 30 mV, it equals RDS(ON) × ILOAD. If the drop reverses past −30 mV (input short or supply failure), DGATE is pulled hard to SOURCE to turn M2 off, which keeps the output capacitor charged. Whenever HGATE pulls low for a fault, DGATE pulls low too.

Seven pins withstand −40 V with respect to GND: VCC, SHDN, UV, OV, HGATE, DGATE and SOURCE. When SOURCE is dragged below GND through a body diode by a negative input or output, both HGATE and DGATE are shorted to SOURCE and both MOSFETs turn off, cutting the path in both directions. OUT and SENSE withstand 20 V below GND.

SHDN below 0.5 V turns off both MOSFETs and the internal circuits, and VCC current drops to 10 µA on both versions. Left open, an internal current source pulls SHDN to about 4 V and the part runs; without a pull-up the pin's leakage must stay at or below 1 µA.

The key figures are RDS(ON), V(BR)DSS, threshold and, for M1, safe operating area. V(BR)DSS must exceed the highest input: with the output shorted or in overvoltage, M1 sees the full input; with the input shorted, M2 sees the held-up output. Gate drive is 10 V to 16 V for VCC above 8 V, so standard-threshold MOSFETs work; below 8 V it can be as low as 5 V and logic-level MOSFETs are needed. On supplies of 24 V or more a 15 V Zener from gate to source on each MOSFET is recommended.

M1's SOA must cover every fault, checked together with the timer capacitor. Surges of 100 ms or longer are governed by heat flow (package, mounting, heat sink) and are analysed with the MOSFET's thermal model; shorter ones are governed by SOA, expressed as P²t, which is roughly constant below 100 ms for a given device but falls as VDS nears its rating. Transient specifications usually take a linear rise tr to VPK and an exponential decay τ: a typical automotive transient is tr = 10 µs, VPK = 80 V, τ = 1 ms; load dump is tr = 5 ms, VPK = 60 V, τ = 200 ms.

The inrush current into the load capacitance is limited by the HGATE slew rate; a capacitor CHG from HGATE to ground slows it further at the cost of slower turn-off. 6.8 nF is the usual value for loop compensation in overvoltage and overcurrent. For input steps faster than 5 V/µs a larger CHG helps stop the MOSFET enhancing itself. Because CHG slows turn-off and lets more current build in a short, a resistor (R6) in series with CHG restores turn-off speed, with a diode (D5) across it, cathode at CHG, giving fast input steps a direct path.

Operation is tested to 80 V and the part is safe from damage between 100 V and −40 V. Supply-trace inductance can produce destructive spikes at VCC, SOURCE and OUT in a short circuit, so power traces should be short and wide. An RC filter at VCC (2.2k and 0.1 µF) removes short spikes; with them, transients up to 250 V shorter than 20 µs are filtered at VCC. A Zener at VCC with the series resistor clamps spikes above 100 V and, in the negative direction, clamps VCC near GND. The resistor raises the minimum input: 2.2k adds about 1 V. For a lasting high input, a depletion-mode MOSFET or an NPN follower replaces the resistor. D3 limits the input to 200 V and blocks D4; D4 keeps SOURCE no lower than 24 V below GND; COUT absorbs the output's inductive energy on an input short.

The output needs at least 22 µF of low-ESR electrolytic capacitance to keep the voltage and current loops stable and to limit how much of an input transient couples through. Ceramic capacitance up to a tenth of the electrolytic total is acceptable. Where the output may go below ground and only ceramics can be used, a 100 mΩ series resistor with them improves stability at light load.

With the output on a connector, plugging it into a supply above the input turns M2 off and stops backfeed. Plugging it into a supply below GND pulls SOURCE below GND through M2's body diode; HGATE is then shorted to SOURCE, turning M1 off and cutting the path from input to output.

Specification: input 8 V to 14 V DC with a 200 V peak transient decaying with τ = 1 ms, output at most 27 V, minimum current limit 4 A, low-battery detection at 6 V, input overvoltage at 60 V, 1 ms early warning. CMZ5945B on VCC keeps VCC below 71 V in the 200 V surge, and its 200 W peak rating at 10/1000 µs covers the 62 mA peak current. M1 must survive an output short at VCC = 14 V; both the hard short and a soft short at 2 V are within the FDB33N25's SOA. For M2 the FDB3682, 36 mΩ maximum at VGS = 10 V and 100 V minimum BVDSS, meets the 45.5 mΩ limit for 5.5 A at 0.25 V drop and handles output transients to 100 V in an input short.

Use Kelvin connections to the sense resistor. Keep the resistance from SOURCE to the MOSFET sources below 10 Ω. On 1 oz copper allow at least 0.02 in of trace width per amp; 1 oz copper has a sheet resistance near 530 µΩ per square, enough to cause large errors at high current. Noise immunity improves greatly when the resistive dividers sit next to their pins and the VCC and GND traces are short.
